title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 313
paragraphs: Of these, Anthylla is a city of note, and is specifically assigned to the wife of the ruler of Egypt to supply her with sandals (this has been the case since the time Egypt came under the Persians); the other city seems to me to take its name from Archander, the son-in-law of Danaus, who was son of Phthios, son of Achaeus; for it is called the City of Archander. There might indeed be another Archander, but in any case the name is not Egyptian.
